heading: INT. COLLAPSED COPPER MINE, CHAMBER 7 - NIGHT

units.text: INT. COLLAPSED COPPER MINE, CHAMBER 7 - NIGHT
A pocket of dark rock, the ceiling low enough to touch.
A single lantern burns blue on the last of the oil.
Dust floats in the beam like drifting ash.
Somewhere beyond the rubble, water drips.
Three miners sit against the walls.
AGNIESZKA PETROVA-LUU (40s, helmet cracked, hands bloodied) tends the lantern.
OLUSEGUN HARTMANN-BELL (30s, wiry, one arm in a makeshift sling) stares at the cave-in.
DOMINGO REYES-ASANTE (60s, gray-faced, a tin lunch pail on his lap) hums an old hymn.
Three days, Segun.
units.name: AGNIESZKA

units.text: Two and a half.
units.name: OLUSEGUN

units.text: We've counted the same.
units.name: AGNIESZKA

units.text: Then we've counted wrong.
units.name: OLUSEGUN

units.text: Hush, both of you. The air.
units.name: DOMINGO

units.text: What about the air?
units.name: AGNIESZKA

units.text: It's thin. Talk less. Think slower.
units.name: DOMINGO

units.text: I can't think slower.
units.name: OLUSEGUN

units.text: Then pray.
units.name: DOMINGO

units.text: To what? To Chamber Seven?
units.name: OLUSEGUN

units.text: Pray to whoever is listening.
units.name: DOMINGO

units.text: Silence.
The lantern sputters.
Agnieszka reaches for the oil can, shakes it.
A thin trickle.
That's the last.
units.name: AGNIESZKA

units.text: Then we're done.
units.name: OLUSEGUN

units.text: We're not done.
units.name: AGNIESZKA

units.text: Agnieszka, we are in a hole.
units.name: OLUSEGUN

units.text: We are in a hole with a lunch pail, a lantern, and an old man who knows every tunnel in this mountain.
units.name: AGNIESZKA

units.text: Every tunnel but this one.
units.name: DOMINGO

units.text: Because it doesn't exist.
units.name: AGNIESZKA

units.text: Because nobody lived to draw it.
units.name: DOMINGO

units.text: A long pause.
Olusegun lowers his head to his knees.
Domingo opens the pail.
Inside, a single boiled egg wrapped in cloth.
He splits it carefully into three pieces.
My wife packed it. She always packs two. I forgot the other this morning.
units.name: DOMINGO

units.text: He passes the pieces.
They eat, slowly, as if tasting something holy.
A faint scrape comes from the rubble.
They freeze.
Another scrape, then a tap, tap, tap, tap.
Rats.
units.name: OLUSEGUN

units.text: Too regular.
units.name: AGNIESZKA

units.text: Quiet.
units.name: DOMINGO

units.text: They scramble toward the wall of stone.
Agnieszka presses her ear to it.
Olusegun scrabbles at a loose rock.
Domingo lifts the lantern.
A stone shifts.
A headlamp stabs through a fist-sized gap, then a hand, then a grimy face: RESCUER JOSIAH WELLINGTON-OKORO (30s, orange helmet, dust-black cheeks), wriggling in on his belly.
Hello? Is anyone alive in here?
units.name: RESCUER

units.text: Olusegun sobs.
Agnieszka laughs.
Domingo closes his eyes and finishes his hymn.
